paragraphs: Here's what this passage teaches, baker. Joash does what is right in the eyes of the LORD "all the days he was instructed by Jehoiada the priest" (2 Kings 12:2). Then comes a Nevertheless: the high places were not removed, and the people kept sacrificing and burning incense there (2 Kings 12:3). Doing right is wonderful, friend, and it's worth asking what might still be left standing in your own life.

Now look at the good stuff, because there's plenty. When the repairs stall, Joash asks the plain question, and Jehoiada answers with a chest, a hole in the lid and honest hands, and the work gets done (2 Kings 12:7-15). The text says no accounting was required "because they acted with integrity" (2 Kings 12:15). That's the kind of baker I want in my kitchen: do the job, do it honestly, and don't make a show of it.

Then Hazael, king of Aram, decides to attack Jerusalem, and Joash sends him the sacred objects and all the gold from the temple and the palace, and Hazael withdraws (2 Kings 12:17-18). The passage ends on a heavy note, with Joash's own servants striking him down (2 Kings 12:20-21). One reign holds the repaired temple, the honest workers, the high places left standing and the gold sent away. That's the big idea, friend: the Word shows people as they are, so let it show you what to keep doing, like the integrity of those workers, and what still needs your attention.
